t: A security-minded NXP chip with two cores, found in open security keys.
steps: Buy an NXP MCU-Link probe, an OKdo E1, or the LPCXpresso55S69 dev board from NXP or a distributor.
Install the free Zephyr tools or the MCUXpresso SDK on your computer.
Install pyOCD to load programs onto the board.
Connect the board to your computer with a micro-USB cable.
Build and flash the Zephyr blinky example for the lpcxpresso55s69 board.
On an OKdo E1, switch the main clock to the internal oscillator before running SDK examples.
Try the Zephyr secure and non-secure samples to see TrustZone at work.
meta: Wild Open. From $13.99. A few stores.
